title: StratosOpX Accessibility Statement
preamble: StratosOpX aims for its website and platform to meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA. Status: partially conformant, pending an independent audit. Bracketed items are placeholders to update once testing is complete.

segments.text: [StratosOpX, LLC] is committed to making its digital products usable by everyone, including people who use screen readers, screen magnifiers, voice control, keyboard-only navigation or other assistive technologies.

items.text: The public website at stratosopx.com, including the pricing page and ROI calculator.
The StratosOpX web platform used by customers, including order review and approval screens, bid analysis results, dashboards and admin settings.
Customer-facing documents we produce, such as go/no-go summaries, compliance checklists and exported reports.

segments.text: Accessibility is part of how we design, build and test, not a one-time project.

rows: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2, Level AA
Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act (for public-sector customers); Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)
Partially conformant: some content does not yet fully meet the standard
Internal review with automated tools and manual keyboard and screen-reader testing; independent third-party audit planned for [Q_ 2027]
Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT 2.5, WCAG and 508 editions) available on request after the audit [target date]

segments.text: We will update this statement after each audit and at least once a year.

blocks.text: 3. Measures we take and accessibility features

items.text: Accessibility requirements are included in design specs and acceptance criteria for new features.
Every release runs automated accessibility checks; key workflows get manual keyboard and screen-reader testing (NVDA and JAWS on Windows, VoiceOver on macOS and iOS).
Team members receive accessibility training, and a named owner tracks issues to resolution.
We consider accessibility when selecting third-party components and vendors.

blocks.text: Features in the website and platform

items.text: Full keyboard navigation with visible focus indicators and skip-to-content links.
Semantic headings, landmarks and labeled form fields for screen readers.
Text contrast of at least 4.5:1, and status (approved, flagged, rejected) shown with text and icons, not color alone.
Layouts that reflow at 400% zoom and support browser text resizing.
Order-review and change-order diff screens that announce changes to assistive technology.
Data tables with proper header markup; charts paired with a text or table alternative.
No time limits on approval tasks, or the ability to extend them; session-timeout warnings with an option to continue.
Exported checklists and reports in accessible, tagged formats (Word, Excel, tagged PDF).

segments.text: We are working to fix the following. [Replace with audit findings once available.]

rows: Purchase orders and RFP packages that customers upload (scanned PDFs, Excel files) are third-party content and may not be accessible
Our extracted, structured view of each document is designed to be accessible; ask support for help
Some interactive sliders may not announce values clearly to all screen readers
Numeric input fields are provided beside each slider
Some complex charts may lack a full text alternative
Export the underlying data to Excel
Third-party scheduling, chat and payment widgets follow their vendors' accessibility practices
Contact us by email or phone instead

segments.text: We do not control the accessibility of customers' ERP systems or other connected third-party products.
If you have trouble using any part of our website or platform, or need content in another format (large print, accessible PDF, Word, plain text, or a walkthrough by phone), please contact us:
